kjv: Now when Jesus was risen early ... (16:9-20, printed as part of Mark without comment)
note: The "longer ending" is absent from Sinaiticus and Vaticanus and unknown to Clement and Origen; Eusebius and Jerome say it was missing from most copies they knew, and its vocabulary and style differ from Mark's. SBLGNT prints it in double brackets as a later addition; KJV presents it as Mark's own text, including the snake-handling and poison promises of 16:17-18. Context: a later addition, kept in double brackets (high confidence). Sinaiticus and Vaticanus end at 16:8; Clement and Origen show no knowledge of 16:9-20; Eusebius and Jerome report it missing from most copies they knew; and its vocabulary, style and abrupt reintroduction of Mary Magdalene (named in 16:1) differ from Mark. Most scholars and SBLGNT judge it an early second-century addition. Other possible meanings: (1) the authentic conclusion of Mark — TR/Majority, A, C, D, W and the great majority of manuscripts, Irenaeus (Against Heresies 3.10.5 cites 16:19), Tatian; KJV, NKJV and defenders such as Burgon, Lunn and Snapp; (2) the Shorter Ending — L, Psi and a few others; (3) Mark's true ending was lost after 16:8 rather than meant to stop there — some scholars.
